articles.title: “Why didn’t they grab her?”: the painful plea of Pamela Cisneros’ mother, the woman shot dead in Times Square
articles.standfirst: The mother of the 49-year-old woman who was shot dead by New York Police officers after stabbing two people in Times Square questioned the officers' actions.
articles.summary: The mother of the 49-year-old woman who was shot dead by New York Police officers after stabbing two people in Times Square questioned the officers' actions.
articles.body:
This Monday, August 31, at around 4:30 p.m., a 49-year-old woman spread panic among citizens and tourists in New York . According to the authorities, Cisneros was carrying two knives and first attacked a 68-year-old man, whom she wounded in the abdomen.

Pamela Cisneros and a resident of the Queens district, shocked everyone by pulling a knife out of a grocery bag and, without hesitation, attacked two people in the abdomen in just 20 seconds. The male victim is in stable condition, according to the New York police. The second victim, a 32-year-old woman, suffered more serious injuries to her abdomen and died at the same hospital.

After the attack, the assailant continued up the street until several officers surrounded her and tried to get her to drop the weapons.

However, Cisneros refused and also threatened to attack the police. The officers even, seeing their lives in danger, first used stun guns. Seeing that they were not effective, they finally opened fire when the woman got even closer to them. The attacker was taken to the hospital, where she later died.

Pamela's mother questioned why the officers resorted to firearms without first trying to physically restrain her. In an interview with Fox 5 News, the woman publicly questioned the NYPD 's actions following her daughter's death and asked: “There were so many police officers… why didn’t they grab her by the arm?”

The situation takes on another dimension because of Cisneros's mental health history. The NYPD confirmed that she had a documented history of interventions related to her mental health in 2018 and 2019, although she had no prior arrests.

Cisneros's brother described her improvement and the family's concern in the days leading up to it

" Patrick Peralta, 59, Cisneros's brother, gave a statement at the place where his mother and stepfather lived and where Cisneros used to spend time. He said he had never seen his sister act violently because of her mental health difficulties. “She was never aggressive,” he emphasized.

According to her brother, Cisneros had gone through difficult years, but in the most recent period her situation seemed to have stabilized.

“She was doing fine, in the last four or five years. She was receiving injections,” Peralta said.

During that period, according to him, his sister lived in an apartment in the Woodside neighborhood and worked intermittently with a lawyer specializing in immigration cases. She had three daughters and a master’s degree in Psychology.

The brother said that the family does not understand what happened. “It was like a switch, and I don’t know what happened in her mind”, he said, adding “We don’t know how to express or explain why this happened. Nothing we say is going to bring that person back. We also feel their pain”

The case left two stories marked by the same episode. On the one hand, the death of Piacenti , a young Bank of America executive who had just returned from maternity leave. On the other, the death of Cisneros, whose family is trying to understand how a woman they describe as stable in recent years ended up carrying out an attack with two knives and dying under police gunfire.

The investigation remains in the hands of specialists and will determine whether the officers' actions were carried out within the protocols established for these circumstances.

articles.title: Sydney Sweeney's daring appearance at the Venice Festival that lives up to her "provocations"
articles.standfirst: The actress is known for her striking looks, which she has already internalized
articles.summary: The actress is known for her striking looks, which she has already internalized
articles.body:
S ydney Sweeney leaves no one indifferent. The actress has been one of the most acclaimed at the Venice Festival , and beyond her acting skills, her appearance always holds some surprise . She has done it again. Everyone has talked about her. Everyone has focused on her. Her way of dressing has caused a sensation among those present because of the outfit she wore.

'The actress posed at the photocall for the party hosted by Armani Beauty at the Festival. As soon as Sweeney stepped onto the red carpet , all eyes were on her, stunning in a silver design that placed it among the most controversial appearances, such as the one at the 2025 Variety"s Power of Women gala.'

In fact, the American artist wore an outfit by the Giorgio Armani brand, which belongs to the label's autumn-winter 2000/01 collection. A design that is transparent with silver sequins, a round neckline, and a black flower on one of the straps . This created a transparent effect that left her underwear visible.

Freedom to dress at the festival and Sweeney takes note

Sweeney had not stepped onto the official Venice Film Festival red carpet until now, something that had not happened since her debut in 2022, when she attended the premiere of "Bones and All," where she posed alongside her Euphoria castmate, Maude Apatow.

Sydney has followed the rule . Because at the festival, guests have complete freedom when it comes to dressing, with a red carpet that sets trends . On this occasion, like Ana de Armas's Marilyn Monroe tribute dress, Dakota Johnson's beaded look, or Zendaya's wet-look design . But Sweeney goes even further, as she usually does.

articles.title: Could anyone live in the world’s most isolated house? The weather explains it all
articles.standfirst: The famous white house on Elliðaey looks like something out of a work of fiction, but its location raises a much harder question to answer.
articles.summary: The famous white house on Elliðaey looks like something out of a work of fiction, but its location raises a much harder question to answer.
articles.body:
There are places that seem made for disappearing from the world. In the middle of the ocean and far from any city, a small white house in Iceland has spent years becoming the perfect image of that idea .

But could it really be as “perfect” as people make it seem?

Honestly, it seems unlikely. To understand why, you first have to look at where the house actually is and, above all, what living in a place like that would really mean.

The house is located on Elliðaey, an island south of Iceland that is part of the Vestmannaeyjar archipelago, which is made up of 18 islands . Across the entire archipelago, only 4,414 people live there , but on Elliðaey, the feeling of isolation is even greater.

And as if the isolation weren’t enough, the weather completely changes the picture of this house

Elliðaey has a subpolar oceanic climate, with low temperatures, high humidity and strong winds throughout much of the year. The ocean and warm currents help moderate the winters, but that doesn’t make the island a place with “nice” weather .

Throughout the year, temperatures generally stay between 33°F and 55°F , with only a few days falling outside that range.

So, what is the long-awaited summer like?

Between June and August, the mildest time of the year arrives, but the word “summer” can be misleading for anyone used to high temperatures .

July is the warmest month, with average highs of around 55°F to 57°F and lows close to 46°F . There is no hot season that turns the island into a beach destination. The cold simply becomes a little less intense.

And winter is another story. Temperatures change drastically, creating much harsher conditions for anyone who is not used to this kind of climate.

So the next time you think about getting away somewhere far from everything, ask yourself first whether the weather will actually be right for it.

articles.title: Musk predicts that humanoid robots will outnumber all humans within 10 years
articles.standfirst: Tesla and SpaceX founder argues that each machine could achieve productivity equivalent to about five people. The forecast requires an industrial leap far beyond the sector's current capabilities.
articles.summary: Tesla and SpaceX founder argues that each machine could achieve productivity equivalent to about five people. The forecast requires an industrial leap far beyond the sector's current capabilities.
articles.body:
E lon Musk e stimates that within ten years there will be more than 1 billion humanoid robots and that each one will be able to achieve productivity equivalent to about five people. The businessman presented this forecast during a virtual address linked to the G20 held on September 1, while speaking about the evolution of artificial intelligence and robotics.

Musk explained that the development of a general-purpose robot will depend on three elements : the artificial intelligence software, the chip it incorporates, and its electromechanical capability. Among its physical capabilities, he especially highlighted the dexterity of its hands, which is necessary for these machines to be able to perform tasks designed for human workers.

A forecast based on productivity

The figure of 1 billion does not mean that robots will outnumber the world’s population. Musk’s estimate is related to the work capacity that those machines could provide.

His estimate is based on the idea that each humanoid could achieve productivity equivalent to that of five people. In that scenario, a fleet of 1 billion robots would have a productive capacity equivalent to about 5 billion workers.

Musk also suggests that the robots themselves could take part in the manufacture of new units. The combination of advances in artificial intelligence, chips, and electromechanical systems would, according to his forecast, make it possible to progressively increase production speed.

This is the entrepreneur's projection and not a consensus estimate about the future of robotics. To reach that scale, the industry would have to radically multiply its manufacturing capacity and reduce the costs of humanoids.

From thousands of robots to more than 1 billion

The gap between Musk's forecast and current industrial capacity is considerable. Hyundai Motor Group aims to have the capacity to manufacture 30,000 robots per year by 2028 as part of its robotics strategy. The group plans to initially use the Atlas humanoids, developed by Boston Dynamics, for industrial tasks such as parts sequencing. Starting in 2030, it envisages expanding their applications to assembly work.

Boston Dynamics , for its part, began manufacturing the production version of Atlas in 2026. The company announced deployments during this year at Hyundai and Google DeepMind facilities.

The figures show the scale of the leap Musk is proposing: moving from industrial production of thousands of units per year to more than 1 billion robots in a decade would require extraordinary growth in manufacturing, in addition to advances in autonomy, artificial intelligence, batteries, sensors, and mechanical components.

Investor interest is also reaching robotics

The sector’s expected growth has also sparked interest among investors. The KraneShares Global Humanoid Robotics and Physical AI Index ETF (KOID) was up 14.70% in 2026 and 23.07% over the last 12 months through August 31, according to data published by KraneShares.

Recent performance, however, has been more uneven: the fund posted a decline of 12.87% in the previous three months. Its net expense ratio stands at 0.69%.

The ETF brings together companies linked to the development of humanoid robots and technologies related to so-called physical intelligence, so its performance offers a reference point for the market’s interest in this topic, although it does not by itself represent the behavior of the entire industry.

The scenario proposed by Musk places the big leap in humanoid robotics around 2036. By then, not only would robots' ability to operate in real-world environments have had to change. Their production would also have had to multiply and their cost be significantly reduced.

The industry has already begun to move in that direction, but current figures are still a long way from the scale proposed by the entrepreneur. Hyundai is targeting an annual capacity of 30,000 units by 2028, while Boston Dynamics is already working with Atlas on its first industrial applications.

Musk's forecast will ultimately depend on whether those technological advances can be turned into mass production in barely a decade.

articles.title: What’s happening with the ozone hole over Antarctica?
articles.standfirst: New report puts the spotlight back on the layer that protects Earth from ultraviolet radiation.
articles.summary: New report puts the spotlight back on the layer that protects Earth from ultraviolet radiation.
articles.body:
For years, the ozone hole over Antarctica was one of those stories that raised alarms every time spring arrived in the Southern Hemisphere. Now, a new report from the World Meteorological Organization has reviewed how it behaved during 2025 and found a detail that is changing the conversation.

A concern that began decades ago

To understand why its recent behavior matters, we first have to go back to the origin of the problem.

The ozone hole appeared as a result of the deterioration of a layer in the atmosphere that protects against the Sun’s ultraviolet radiation. Among the substances responsible were chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) , which were used for decades in refrigeration, air conditioning, aerosols and other products.

When these compounds reach the stratosphere, they can release chlorine and bromine, which take part in reactions capable of destroying ozone.

The situation prompted countries to act together and, in 1987, the Montreal Protocol was adopted , with the goal of gradually phasing out substances that damaged the ozone layer.

The change became visible over time

The recovery of the ozone layer could not happen overnight. The damage had already been done, and some of the substances that contributed to its deterioration could remain in the atmosphere for years, so the process would inevitably take time.

According to the WMO , the ozone layer began showing signs of recovery around 2000, although the process could take several decades before returning to levels similar to those seen before its deterioration.

And precisely because this recovery has not been a straight line, some of the changes recorded in recent years have begun to draw attention.

2025 recorded one of the smallest ozone holes

The WMO’s Ozone Bulletin says the ozone hole observed in 2025 was among the smallest recorded since 1992 , when severe depletion patterns began to be observed.

The report ranks it as the fourth- or fifth-smallest of that period. It was also the second consecutive year in which both its size and depth were significantly below the average recorded between 1990 and 2010.

Although those figures pointed toward recovery, 2026 once again showed that the ozone hole can change from one year to the next. During the first weeks of September, it grew rapidly, and on September 12, it reached 25 million square kilometers .

That figure was about 5 million square kilometers above the seasonal average, although it was still well below the record of 29.6 million km² set in 2006 .

But there is an important detail: this increase does not mean that the chemicals that damaged the ozone layer have returned. Scientists have linked it to extreme weather conditions, particularly a sudden drop in temperatures in the stratosphere over the South Pole, which favored the formation of Polar Stratospheric Clouds .

articles.title: 4 astronomical events you won’t want to miss before September ends
articles.standfirst: September is almost over, but the sky still has a few moments that might make you stop and look up.
articles.summary: September is almost over, but the sky still has a few moments that might make you stop and look up.
articles.body:
T here are only a few days left before September comes to an end, and fall is practically here . But before the season changes, there are still several reasons to take a moment and look toward the sky.

Venus will have one of its brightest nights

On September 22, Venus will reach one of the most striking moments of the month as it reaches its greatest brightness of the year.

The planet will be visible to the naked eye shortly after sunset, toward the west, where it will appear as an especially bright white point . You won’t need a telescope to find it, making this one of those opportunities when all you have to do is look up at the right time.

The date will also have another significance: around the same time, the fall equinox will arrive, officially marking the change of seasons in the Northern Hemisphere. The exact moment of the equinox will be at 12:05 a.m. UTC on September 23 , meaning it will take place during the night of September 22 into September 23, depending on your time zone.

Mars will have some very special company

Three days later, on September 25, it will be time to look toward another part of the sky.

Before sunrise, toward the east, Mars will appear alongside Castor and Pollux, the two brightest stars in the constellation Gemini. The planet, recognizable by its reddish color, will form a visual alignment with them .

This does not mean that the three objects will actually be aligned in space. From our perspective on Earth, however, they will appear to line up, creating a particularly striking scene for anyone who enjoys watching the sky before sunrise .

And just as September enters its final days, an even more special night will arrive.

The Harvest Moon will appear alongside Saturn

September 26 will likely be the date that catches the attention of those who prefer looking at the sky after sunset.

The Harvest Moon, the traditional name for the full moon closest to the fall equinox , will reach full illumination and appear in the eastern sky shortly after sunset.

Saturn will be visible very close to the Moon, creating a pair that should be relatively easy to spot with the naked eye . For those who don’t regularly follow astronomical events, this could be one of the simplest scenes to look for during the final days of September: wait for nightfall and look toward the east.

And that same night, another planet will be waiting nearby, although finding it will be much more difficult.

Neptune will be nearby too, but you’ll have to look for it

On September 26, Neptune will reach opposition , a moment when it will be in a particularly favorable position for observation from Earth.

But this is where the experience changes completely.

Unlike Venus, Mars or Saturn, Neptune is too faint to be seen with the naked eye. You’ll need binoculars or a telescope to locate it, where it may appear as a tiny bluish point.

That night, Neptune will also be in the same area of the sky as the Moon and Saturn, creating a sort of visual triangle . However, while the other two objects should be relatively easy to spot, Neptune will require a little more patience and the right equipment.

And perhaps that is part of the appeal of these final days of September: not every event is meant to be viewed in quite the same way.

articles.title: Serena Williams' husband faces accusations of exploiting female athletes: this was his response
articles.standfirst: Alexis Ohanian defended the Athlos model against questions about his business in women's sports and proposed a structure in which some athletes also have an ownership stake in the league.
articles.summary: Alexis Ohanian defended the Athlos model against questions about his business in women's sports and proposed a structure in which some athletes also have an ownership stake in the league.
articles.body:
" The business of Alexis Ohanian in women's sports became the center of an uncomfortable discussion. Serena Williams' husband was accused of exploiting athletes through Athlos , the women's track and field competition he created, and decided to respond by focusing on one of the main features of his project.

For Ohanian , the issue is not just about how much an athlete is paid to compete. His bet is that some of them may be able to have a stake in ownership of the league itself and, in that way, also benefit if the value of the business increases.

The detail Ohanian uses to defend himself

Athlos introduced for 2026 a model of athlete ownership, through which certain athletes have a stake in the organization. Among the figures linked to the project are Gabby Thomas, Tara Davis-Woodhall, and Sha"Carri Richardson .

That is precisely one of the arguments used to defend the model against the criticism: the athletes would not only be the protagonists of a spectacle created by third parties, but some would also have a financial stake in its growth.

Athlos also increased the prizes

The project announced more than US$2.1 million in prize money for its two 2026 competitions. The winner of each event receives US$65,000 , while the overall champions also receive a US$25,000 bonus.

Athlos thus seeks to build a sports property with greater commercial appeal and compete for the attention of an audience that has historically received fewer offerings focused exclusively on women's athletics.

The business that started after a warning from Serena

Ohanian's bet also has a personal component. The businessman said that Serena Williams tried to dissuade him from investing in women's sports because she knew firsthand the economic and structural difficulties female athletes face.

Ohanian decided to move forward anyway and made women's sports an important part of his investment strategy. Athlos is now his most visible project in athletics.

That is why the accusations against the businessman open up a discussion that goes beyond his figure: Who should keep the money when women's sports become an increasingly bigger business?

articles.title: Shakira's concerts in Madrid leave a wave of complaints: "It was scary"
articles.standfirst: The public's response to the musical show has been positive, although some attendees have questioned the access points, the waits inside the venue, and the perceived movement in the stands.
articles.summary: The public's response to the musical show has been positive, although some attendees have questioned the access points, the waits inside the venue, and the perceived movement in the stands.
articles.body:
T he Shakira concerts in Madrid have been well received by her fans, although some attendees have reported long waits and have expressed concern about the movement of the stands.

The complaints focused mainly on the long queues to access Macondo Park and on the waits to buy food. Added to these problems were comments from spectators who said they had noticed movement in the stands during the concert, a situation that caused concern among part of the audience.

The venue, a theme park of about 30 hectares, is hosting a total of 12 concerts with which the Colombian singer will bring her Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran tour to an end on October 11. More than 50,000 people attend each night, a figure that gives an idea of the logistical challenge each day entails.

Concern among part of the audience

A young woman who attended one of the concerts said that the movement of the stands was especially noticeable during the show. “The stands were moving a lot with people’s movements. It was terrifying. No one was dancing because people were so scared. Some people suffered anxiety attacks and had to be treated by the venue’s medical services”, she explained.

Other accounts emphasized long lines to enter the venue and also the waits to buy food

Live Nation Spain responded to the comments with a statement published on X . The promoter responsible for the performances stated that the facilities comply with the established safety checks.

“All our structures, including the stands, are duly certified and officially checked for their safety and stability,” the company said.

The first concert was a success musically, but it left doubts regarding organization , with an overall picture in which the enthusiasm of the fans coexists with criticism over the management of access, services, and the stands.

The artist still has ten concerts ahead in the capital: September 20, 25, 26 and 27; October 2, 3, 4, 9, 10 and 11. All of them are being held at Macondo Park

articles.title: Summer is saying goodbye to the U.S.: Here’s what fall will bring
articles.standfirst: The new season is about to begin, and the weather won’t behave the same way across every region of the country.
articles.summary: The new season is about to begin, and the weather won’t behave the same way across every region of the country.
articles.body:
Summer is slowly fading into the background, and the United States is getting ready for a change of season . September can still feel like an extension of the warmer months, but the calendar shows that fall is just around the corner.

When does fall begin in the United States?

Fall begins on Tuesday, September 22, 2026, marking the change of season that will bring new temperatures , different days and, little by little, the landscapes typically associated with this time of year.

But beyond putting away summer clothes or getting the sweaters back out, this transition also raises a much more practical question: what will the weather be like over the next few months?

The outlook for October, November and December points to significant differences across the country . In other words, not every American will have the same kind of fall ahead.

Temperatures could feel warmer across several regions

One of the main trends in the outlook points to above-average temperatures across much of the United States.

The West, the northern part of the country and regions east of the Mississippi River are among the areas showing a stronger tendency toward warmer-than-usual temperatures during these months.

That does not mean every day will feel the same or that cold weather will disappear. It is a broader seasonal outlook, so actual conditions can vary from week to week and from one city to another.

And while much of the map points toward a warmer-than-usual fall, the South presents a much less defined scenario.

Some Southern states still have an uncertain outlook

Texas, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Colorado, Arkansas and Louisiana are among the regions where the probabilities appear more evenly balanced.

In these states, the outlook does not clearly favor warmer or colder temperatures than normal. As a result, residents could experience different conditions as the season progresses .

That difference is important because there is no single forecast for the entire United States. While some areas have a clearer climate signal, others still have several possible outcomes .

But temperatures won’t be the only change worth watching.

The South could see more rain this fall

When it comes to precipitation, the outlook becomes much clearer.

A trend toward above-average rainfall across much of the South is expected, in a stretch that extends from Southern California toward the eastern part of the country and reaches the Mid-Atlantic region. Florida is among the states showing a particularly strong signal for increased precipitation .

For people living in these areas, that could mean a fall with more rainy days than usual.

But while some regions may need to reach for their umbrellas more often, other parts of the country are pointing in the opposite direction.

The Pacific Northwest could have a drier fall

The contrast is more noticeable in the Pacific Northwest and part of the Great Lakes region , where models point toward drier-than-usual conditions.

And behind much of this outlook is a climate phenomenon that will be particularly important in the months ahead.

What does El Niño have to do with fall 2026?

The expected pattern for the season is connected to the development of El Niño, a climate phenomenon that can influence atmospheric patterns and the distribution of temperatures and precipitation.

According to NOAA, there is a greater than 90% chance that the event will reach a very strong intensity during the fall and winter of 2026-2027 . The projected scenario also has a 75% chance of matching or exceeding the intensity of some of the strongest events recorded since 1950.

One of the effects expected from this pattern is a shift in the jet stream, which helps explain why the outlook shows such noticeable differences from one region to another.

articles.title: Chad Gilbert Cause of death: New Found Glory guitarist dies; three months earlier he had returned to performing live
articles.standfirst: The guitarist and co-founder of New Found Glory died on September 20, surrounded by his family. In June, he had returned to the stage after undergoing emergency brain surgery.
articles.summary: The guitarist and co-founder of New Found Glory died on September 20, surrounded by his family. In June, he had returned to the stage after undergoing emergency brain surgery.
articles.body:
"Chad Gilbert, guitarist and co-founder of New Found Glory, died on Sunday, September 20 at the age of 45 after several years of battling cancer. His wife, Lisa Cimorelli, and the band members announced the news and noted that the musician passed away in his sleep , accompanied by family members and loved ones. The cause of death has not yet been specified.

The death occurred three months after one of the most significant moments of his final years: his return to the stage. In June, Gilbert performed again with New Found Glory in Nashville, where he played guitar from a motorized scooter.

An illness that became complicated in 2026

Gilbert had been diagnosed in 2021 with metastatic pheochromocytoma, a rare tumor related to the adrenal glands. Over the following years, he received various treatments and underwent several procedures as the disease spread to other parts of his body.

In February 2026, the musician collapsed at home and had to undergo emergency brain surgery.

After the operation, he explained that his diagnosis had changed to stage 4 adrenocortical carcinoma . Until then, he had received different treatments, including immunotherapy, to fight the tumors affecting his body.

Despite his health condition, Gilbert returned to the stage on June 8 during a New Found Glory concert in Nashville. He took part in songs such as "Hit or Miss" and "My Friends Over You" from a motorized scooter. After the performance, he said he had been able to play in front of his daughter Lily, something he was not sure he would be able to do again.

“I had the opportunity to perform a concert in front of my daughter, something I never thought I would do again,” Gilbert wrote on Instagram referring to his daughter Lily after the concert. He also thanked “all the nurses and doctors, my incredible team that has kept me alive during my fight.”

Almost three decades with New Found Glory

Gilbert co-founded New Found Glory in 1997 and was one of the band's central figures for nearly three decades. As a guitarist, songwriter, and backing vocalist, he took part in more than a dozen albums and numerous international tours.

The group highlighted his musical and personal contribution after news of his death became known. In the joint statement with Cimorelli, his bandmates noted that his guitar playing, his compositions, his humor, and his dedication helped define New Found Glory throughout all those years.

Gilbert also worked as a producer with other bands from the punk and hardcore scene and developed side projects, including What's Eating Gilbert and International Superheroes of Hardcore . New Found Glory, meanwhile, achieved one of its greatest successes with the album Sticks and Stones, released in 2002.

'Months before his death, Gilbert had spoken about his family and professional life in an interview. "I lived my dream thanks to my family and to having been able to do so many creative things," he said, referring to his wife, his daughter, and the chance to have devoted his life to music. '

articles.title: They are seeking a restraining order against Dolly Parton's nephew for threatening her $450 million inheritance
articles.standfirst: The company that manages the estate of the late country singer is behind the petition
articles.summary: The company that manages the estate of the late country singer is behind the petition
articles.body:
Inheritances often cause problems, and Dolly Parton's case seems to be no exception. The company managing the late country star's estate has requested a restraining order against Bryan Seaver, the artist's nephew , after accusing him of making serious threats of violence and destruction of her commercial legacy .

The conflict has erupted in a Nashville court just one month after the death of the American singer, who died of cancer at the age of 80, leaving an estimated fortune of 450 million dollars. Bryan Seaver served for more than two decades as the head of security for the singer's properties ; however, following Parton's death, the management company decided to fire him and remove him from his duties due to alleged "intimidating conduct".

Parton's nephew claims his words were “taken out of context”

"As a result of his dismissal, tensions increased and the administrators turned to the courts by presenting evidence of the hostile messages sent by Seaver . According to the lawsuit, the legendary singer's nephew demanded money payments under the threat of destroying his aunt's business empire and boycotting her brand collaborations.

In the collected texts, he boasted of having experience abroad with military contractors during the Iraq War and even went so far as to call himself an "international arms dealer." In this way, the fear generated led to the resignation of the estate trusts attorney, the departure of several employees, and the need to hire private security to protect staff in their own homes.

After the lawsuit became public in media outlets such as the American portal TMZ, Bryan Seaver defended himself by claiming that his words had been "taken out of context" . He stated that the messages were exchanged in a private atmosphere of deep frustration and said he was dismayed by his sudden dismissal. In addition, he stressed that his only real intention continues to be "protecting his family" .

articles.title: Shakira spotted having dinner with a mysterious companion in Madrid: "Very affectionate"
articles.standfirst: The Colombian singer continues with her grand debut in the capital these weeks with her concerts
articles.summary: The Colombian singer continues with her grand debut in the capital these weeks with her concerts
articles.body:
Shakira, one of the most prominent singers on the international music scene, is moving forward with her 12 concerts in Madrid as part of her ‘Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour’. The Colombian performer kicked off her run at the Shakira Stadium , in Villaverde, on September 18, 19, and 20, and will continue on the 25th, 26th, and 27th of this month, and October 2, 3, 4, 9, 10, and 11.

However, beyond delighting her fans with her countless hits, according to ‘El verano se mueve’, a Telecinco program presented by Ion Aramendi and Kike Quintana, she was photographed arriving at a restaurant in the capital alongside a man whose identity and the reasons for the evening remain completely unknown.

This is the man who accompanied Shakira

Sergio Garrido , a contributor to the aforementioned Mediaset program, was the one who brought the snapshots to the format, recounting the details of this meeting. In the images, Shakira can be seen dressed entirely in black, getting out of a car and heading toward the Madrid restaurant.

In another snapshot, you can see a man dressed in a white shirt, but with his face pixelated , captured at the same frontage. Garrido, also a photographer, revealed that it could have been a simple and discreet dinner, but according to him, it was not: “They were together for almost the entire dinner and very affectionate, talking constantly".

Likewise, this dinner would have taken place entirely in secret , but the singer herself realized that she was being followed, according to the version told by the paparazzo on Telecinco's afternoon magazine show: “Just look at how lovey-dovey they were that she asked to change tables because I was behind a curtain," he pointed out , assuring that both of them were acting very affectionately.

articles.title: Mariah Medina reports that a judge reprimanded her for wearing a sleeveless dress in the middle of the courtroom "inappropriate attire"
articles.standfirst: The former television reporter and current criminal defense attorney claims that the judge asked her to approach the bench to inspect her attire in front of other lawyers and defendants.
articles.summary: The former television reporter and current criminal defense attorney claims that the judge asked her to approach the bench to inspect her attire in front of other lawyers and defendants.
articles.body:
Mariah Medina reported that a judge questioned her clothing during a hearing in a Bexar County court. According to her account, the judge considered a gray sleeveless dress that left her arms exposed to be inappropriate and asked her to approach the bench so it could be examined more closely in front of other lawyers and defendants.

The incident occurred during a brief hearing and was later recounted by the lawyer on her X account , where she also posted a photograph of the dress. The garment, she explained, had already been worn on numerous occasions during her time as a journalist and in other courtrooms without anyone objecting to its appearance. Her post also sparked numerous reactions on social media about dress codes in courtrooms.

The dress that sparked the conflict

The garment is a gray straight-cut sleeveless J.Crew dress with a length close to the knee . After the judge questioned her appearance, Medina explained that it was a shift dress.

According to her account, the judge laughed and asked her whether she really considered that clothing appropriate for a jury trial and whether she had a jacket in her car.

In her post, the attorney also questioned the way the reprimand was delivered. "She made me turn around at the bench so she could see my outfit… in front of the defendants and the other attorneys", she wrote. Medina described the situation as disappointing and noted that it was the first time she had faced an episode of this kind since she was licensed to practice.

What the regulation establishes

The rules of the Bexar County criminal courts establish that attorneys and judicial officers must wear formal attire during sessions. The regulations also provide for the possibility of wearing business casual attire when the corresponding judge permits it, so there is room for discretion within each courtroom.

According to Medina herself, the dress did not violate the rules that were posted at the entrance to the courtroom.

The lawyer also posted an old video in which she appears wearing the same garment during her time as a journalist and stated that she did not regret having worn it. At the same time, she acknowledged that she would wear a jacket if necessary to appear before that judge.

articles.title: Harvest Moon 2026: When is it and what time will the full moon of September 2026 be visible?
articles.standfirst: The last full moon of September will light up the US sky this weekend and will arrive accompanied by other protagonists of the Solar System.
articles.summary: The last full moon of September will light up the US sky this weekend and will arrive accompanied by other protagonists of the Solar System.
articles.body:
The 2026 Harvest Moon will light up the U.S. sky this weekend, accompanied by a special companion: Saturn. The full moon will reach its peak on Saturday, September 26, at 12:49 p.m. EDT, meaning the exact moment of fullness will occur during the day.

However, those wishing to enjoy the spectacle will have to wait until nightfall. The Harvest Moon will appear above the eastern horizon at sunset on Saturday, when it begins to rise and becomes visible to the naked eye, weather permitting.

When to see the 2026 Harvest Moon?

Although the exact moment of the full moon falls on Saturday afternoon, the moon will appear virtually full for several nights.

In the United States, the best time to view it will be at nightfall on Saturday, September 26 , as the Moon rises in the east. Near the horizon, it may take on a yellow, golden, or orange hue due to the way light passes through Earth's atmosphere.

The phenomenon can also be enjoyed on the nights of Friday, September 25, and Sunday, September 27, though the Moon will be slightly further removed from the exact moment of fullness.

Key facts about the 2026 Harvest Moon:

Date: Saturday, September 26.

Lighting during the day: about 99.7%.

Departure direction: approximately East.

Favorable period: nights of September 25 to 27.

What other planets will accompany the full moon in September 2026?

The Moon will not be alone during this late September. Saturn will be visible in the night sky and can be observed with the naked eye under favorable conditions, while Neptune will require powerful binoculars or a telescope due to its low apparent brightness.

To enjoy the lunar phenomenon, no instrument will be necessary. It will be enough to look for a place with few artificial lights and a clear horizon.

Why is it called the Harvest Moon?

September's full moon is traditionally known as the Harvest Moon because it is the one that occurs closest to the autumn equinox in the Northern Hemisphere.

The name relates to the time of year when farmers historically took advantage of the moonlight to extend their workday and gather crops before nightfall.

Saturn will accompany the Moon

One of the highlights of the night will be the presence of Saturn near the Moon. The ringed planet can be spotted in the sky as a bright, yellowish point of light, positioned roughly below the Moon.

The apparent proximity of these two celestial bodies offers a great opportunity to view them together. With a telescope, it will be possible to make out Saturn's distinctive rings in greater detail.

How can you see the Harvest Moon?

No special equipment is needed to enjoy this phenomenon. You simply need to find a location with a clear horizon and minimal light pollution, particularly toward the east.

It is recommended to be ready at sunset on Saturday, September 26, to watch the Moon rise. During its first few minutes above the horizon, the Moon can take on a particularly striking appearance due to atmospheric effects and the "Moon illusion," which makes it appear larger when it is close to the horizon.

The exact time of moonrise depends on your location, so it is best to check the local moonrise time when planning your viewing.

articles.title: World’s highest-IQ man says he has concluded ‘God is real’
articles.standfirst: Scientists and psychologists caution that intelligence alone does not determine the validity of a claim about religion
articles.summary: Scientists and psychologists caution that intelligence alone does not determine the validity of a claim about religion
articles.body:
The centuries-old debate over the existence of God has attracted philosophers, theologians and scientists from virtually every era. Now, one man widely recognized for possessing an exceptionally high IQ is adding his voice to the conversation.

YoungHoon Kim, a South Korean scientist who has been recognized by organizations including the Giga Society for achieving an extraordinarily high IQ score, recently drew attention after posting a series of statements on social media declaring his belief in God, Jesus and the Bible. In one post shared on X, Kim wrote: " As the world's highest IQ record holder, I finally concluded that God is real, Jesus is real, and the Bible is real. 100%."

In a separate video, he appeared wearing a cross necklace and stated, "Jesus is the answer. He is coming soon. 100%." The comments generated a discussion among both religious communities and those interested in the intersection of science and faith.

Intelligence and belief are not the same thing

Kim's remarks have attracted attention partly because of his reported IQ score of 276, a figure that would place him far above the range typically associated with giftedness. For comparison, an IQ score of around 100 is generally considered average, while scores above 140 are often categorized as exceptionally high.

Yet scientists and psychologists caution that intelligence alone does not determine the validity of a claim about religion, philosophy or metaphysics. Questions surrounding God's existence are not scientific questions in the traditional sense because they cannot currently be tested or falsified through experiments.

As a result, beliefs about God are often shaped by personal experiences, philosophical arguments, cultural backgrounds and theological traditions rather than IQ scores. In other words, Kim's statements are significant because of who made them, but they remain personal conclusions rather than scientific findings.

A long-standing interest in theology

Kim's recent comments are not a sudden departure from his previous views. Over the years, he has frequently spoken about Christianity and the role faith plays in his life. He has previously posted statements expressing belief in Jesus and has described Christianity as central to his worldview.

His interest in religion extends beyond personal belief. Kim also holds a theology degree from Yonsei University in Seoul and has referred to theology as "the ultimate discipline of all fields of study." That educational background may help explain why he often approaches questions of faith through both philosophical and intellectual lenses.

Kim has also discussed the possibility of an afterlife, arguing that certain ideas from quantum physics and consciousness studies can be viewed as compatible with religious concepts. In previous remarks, he suggested that if reality is part of a larger framework than humans currently understand, death might represent a transition rather than an ending.

Such ideas are not uncommon among thinkers exploring the relationship between science and spirituality. However, they remain speculative and are not considered established scientific conclusions. Many physicists caution that concepts from quantum mechanics are frequently invoked in discussions of consciousness and religion without direct experimental evidence linking them to life after death or supernatural phenomena.
